title: Ai Cooked and your upset?
author: Z1supercpu
selftext: This post is for anyone that is not able to understand what is currently happening with video games, and to reply to people who are upset that They cannot definitively break down terms that are used today. Because I have pointed out lazy people and people who literally just want to ship their games and post about how many wishlists they received, I get people who argue the idea of Ai slop. Unfortunately they don’t understand that it’s humans that push dominoes and people who iterate or correct Ai and still blame a computer for their lack of creativity, and the fact that undeveloped one shot prompt or games made from single text captures don’t come out well. Then the games are pushed by a person to the market or to harass you through ads. I really feel bad for people that can’t understand this and still show ignorance by terming it Ai slop, yes the computer made it but your missing the point that You want to blame a six year old for artwork when their parents sell it? Who is more responsible for putting out a bad product? Exactly. I removed my posts in the past so not influence the general public because the ignorance had led me to believe that they don’t deserve to have such knowledge and now, I find it deserving to claim intelligence so that the ones lacking can understand how they are wrong. Also for those that use consistent thinking will agree on this thought. So I figure there will always be people that want to speak to cover their faults and that is what this argument is, don’t tell me how many wishlists you have, or that Ai slop is ruining games, because it’s not, it’s actually a bridge to people that didn’t have the ability to goto school and learn code to make things they can now, and if you went to school, great then where are your games your so proud of? Don’t send me a screen shot of 2d games that have no curb appeal.

comments.author: jaykal001
comments.body:
AI has limitations, and people have limitations.  There's ways for them to co-exist and work well together.  Whether that be better tooling, better prompting, whatever - I don't have all the answers.

Where I personally struggle is the idea that someone spent a day, a week, whatever - prompting the AI clone of xxxx - and we are just supposed to buy that it's as good as the original.  I think we're in a weird point in time where we seen people trying to clone > release > make $100, and repeating.  Those types of developers seem to be pushing "slop" to make a quick buck, and it ruins it for people trying to learn, experiment, explore.  AI isn't the issue - people are.  They always are lol

comments.author: TheBoxGuyTV
comments.body:
I agree with you conceptually.

People are more against AI for interpersonal reasons. For self identity rather than the legitimate results.

We can agree that AI slop is a thing and its like you said, the result of people using AI and not actually refining it in a meaningful way due to laziness, inexperience (skill and intuition) or time constraints.

I imagine more people are using AI in their games than they want to admit and some people literally make post about how they used AI and then transitioned to their own or another person's work (code, art etc.).

I use AI in my game in some of my coding. I don't use it for art or audio because I don't find it useful for my situation. AI is amazing at creating walls of text and adjusting my code to maintain formatting, adding small adjustments like when I used it to implement my color pallet code, instead of manually and search changing my code, I used AI to produce the outcome based on how I imagined it. It was literally an array for each color constant and then me using another variable to represent the active pallet.

Here is what it looks like:

cl_blue = [blue, blue, blue]

Here the 3 indexes represent a different blue to match a specific stylization. I then use an index representative variable to set the proper colors. This is an easy way for me to implement color pallets and eventually add in color blindness settings. When I do that, I'll just use AI to add in new indexes to represent those new pallets. I don't need to waste time manually creating new colors. I simply will test them and adjust myself as needed. This saved me hours of trial and error.

It also helps me create redundant data sets where I cannot use abstraction in a meaningful way. 

Example I have a master tool/item struct that defines the default values for my reference system. This system runs at the start of my game and auto builds structs and then I used an AI by feeding it my enums that represent tools and items to make me the code block representing all my tools and items. Instead of typing and copy/pasting the structs per individual item/tool. Of course I also made shared data sets where defaults aren't enough and where unique elements are shared among other items. This reference system handles data for tools, crafting, item behavior, world and UI presentation, shops etc. Its a lot of data to type out. So I made AI create the bones of each item and I basically applied some abstraction to implant overrides where needed or manually enter very specific information as needed.

I have even used it to create a system I wasnt sure how to make but I prefer to avoid this because it makes it difficult to troubleshoot  as AI doesn't code like I do.

Also I have had to correct the AI in its approach due to it over complicating something or adding double work because it wasn't aware or ignored existing architecture.

replies.body: Thank you for your honest reply, exactly as my post said you have an understanding to what the issues are, and using ai as the tool it’s intended to be, I as well currently have a game conceptually and the amount of time saved or the ability to construct the concept what may have taken month or years is able to be accomplished in a 45 day span of working with battle systems mechanics overlays and understanding how the game will operate and the finished idea, it’s amazing because I am not someone who spent my time chasing money but this is an opportune time to put out a good product as well as benefiting from it, though the main thought was to out do companies that are lacking in areas and giving consumers what they have wanted. Each day I see more refined projects and videos of what Ai is doing and basically the brick wall of technology isn’t so much as a block but a checkpoint to what is going to be next, and this is a turning point that we are living in. I am looking forward to what other people put out and if they have a great idea I’ll buy and play the game so if I don’t make my own. But the concept I have I am confident in.
